label: Fairino FR20
_comment_frames: Same three frames as uf850.json -- configurejoints, extracted, robot.
The rest skeleton is BUILT from the vendor URDF by scripts/urdf_rig.py
at the URDF zero pose, rather than read from an FBX. That is why sign and
offset are trivial here: every joint's KineFX frame was constructed so
that turning the URDF joint by +q turns the KineFX joint by +q about the
listed axis. urdf_rig.py's tests measure this per joint (+25 deg in,
+25 deg out) instead of asserting it.
URDF zero == controller zero, confirmed against SimMachine set to
FR20-V1-001 (V6.0): the controller's GetForwardKin and this URDF agree to
0.016 mm and 0.0006 deg over 23 poses, flange face 120 mm past joint_6.

robot._comment_limits: From fairino20_v6.urdf (vendor, frcobot_ros2/fairino_description). Robot frame, degrees. To be cross-checked against the controller's own soft limits.
robot._comment_velocity: Per joint, from Fairino's FR20 datasheet (fairino.us product page): J1-J3 +-120 deg/s, J4-J6 +-180 deg/s; TCP up to 2 m/s. The URDF's 180.5 / 183.3 deg/s look like placeholders and are not used. The controller's own safety settings (collaborative speed limits) may cap lower; the asset's Max Joint Velocity parameter caps every joint on top of these.

rig._comment_source: No FBX. The asset builds the rest skeleton and link meshes from this URDF itself (urdf_skeleton / urdf_links, through scripts/urdf_rig.py); nothing needs wiring into input 0.
rig._comment_flange: Distance along joint_6's +Y from the joint to the tool mounting face. FR20's last joint sits behind the face: 0.120 m, measured as the far extent of wrist3_link.STL along the link's own axis (urdf_rig.flange_offset_from_mesh; urdf_rig.py's tests hold this number to that measurement). The asset moves the TCP by this much before applying any tool.
rig._comment_axis: Measured from geometry by urdf_rig.build_rest_skeleton: 'y' where the URDF axis lies along the bone (J1 vertical, and J4/J5/J6 whose next joint sits along their own axis), 'z' where it is perpendicular (J2, J3 -- the two hinges).
rig._comment_sign: robot = extracted * sign. All +1 by construction; verified per joint in urdf_rig.py's tests.
rig._comment_offset: Skeleton built at the URDF zero, so extracted angles start at zero. URDF zero == controller zero, confirmed in SimMachine (FR20-V1-001 V6.0): GetForwardKin matches this URDF to 0.016 mm and 0.0006 deg over 23 poses.
rig._comment_fbik: J4: MEASURED false. An IK solve to a manual goal of joint_6 rest + (0.9, 0.2, -0.4) m in joint_6's local frame returned J4 = +95.67 deg against a configured range of [-265, 85] -- the same silent over-limit seen on UF850's J4. The other five are NOT yet probed; true means unverified, not confirmed.
rig._comment_ik: FR20 is a UR-type arm (J2/J3/J4 parallel -- measured), so it solves with scripts/ur_ik.py's closed form instead of KineFX Full Body IK, which jams on ranges crossing +-180 and at wrist flips. Branches are filtered by the Solve tab presets, then the one nearest the previous frame wins; with no previous frame, nearest ik_reference_deg.

output._comment_writer: No Fairino-specific writer exists yet. The CSV columns (time_s, j1_deg..j6_deg) are controller-neutral; how the Fairino side consumes them is still open.
output._comment_cap: Copied from uf850.json as a conservative default. Its meaning for a Fairino export is not defined yet.

presets._comment: Robot frame. Converted to the configurejoints frame at apply time.

shoulder._comment_back: J1 stops at +-175, so the true 'back' region is split across +-180 and cannot be one range. This is its +J1 half only.

elbow._comment_side: Measured with forward kinematics: while the arm reaches forward (J2 between -90 and 0), J3 > 0 puts the elbow ABOVE the shoulder-wrist line. Leaning past vertical (J2 < -90) flips it -- the usual reason industrial elbow flags are read together with the shoulder flag.
